His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾. Al-kashṭ means pulling off with great adhesion. So the sky is stripped away as the hide is stripped from a ram or other animal. Al-qashṭ is a dialectal form of it. In Abdullah's reading: "And when the sky is stripped." I stripped the camel's hide (kashṭan): I removed its skin. It is not said "salakhtuh" (I flayed it), because the Arabs say about the camel only "kashaṭtuhu" or "jaladtuhu." "Inkashaṭa" means it went away. So the sky is pulled from its place as a covering is pulled from a thing. It was also said: it is folded, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the day We fold up the sky like the folding of the scroll for the books﴾ [al-Anbiya: 104]. So the meaning is: it is uprooted and then folded. And Allah knows best.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Hellfire is set ablaze﴾: that is, it is kindled and set aflame for the disbelievers, and its heat is increased. It is said: "sa''altu al-nar" and "asta'altuha" (I kindled the fire). The reading of the majority is with the light form, from "al-sa'ir" (the blaze). Nafi', Ibn Dhakwan and Ruways read it with the shaddah, because it was kindled repeatedly, time after time. Qatadah said: Its kindling was caused by the anger of Allah and the sins of the children of Adam. In al-Tirmidhi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The Fire was kindled for a thousand years until it became red, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became white, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became black; so it is black and dark." It is also narrated as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: that is, it draws near and comes close to the God-fearing. Al-Hasan said: They will be brought close to it, not that it will move from its place. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd used to say: "It was adorned…"[[In Z: "it was brought near."]] — "uzlifat?" And "al-zulfa" in the language of the Arabs is nearness, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 90]. And "tazallafa fulan" means he drew near.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Every soul will know what it has presented﴾, meaning what it did of good and evil. This is the answer to "When the sun is wrapped up" and what follows it. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: For this the narration was ordered. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that they recited it, and when they reached "Every soul will know what it has presented," they said: "For this the narrative was arranged." So the meaning according to this is: "When the sun is wrapped up," and these things happen, "every soul will know what it has presented of its deeds." In the two Sahihs, from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is none among you but Allah will speak to him, with no interpreter between them. He will look to his right and see nothing but what he has sent forth, and he will look to his left and see nothing but what he has sent forth [and he will look to his left and see nothing but what he has sent forth]. Then the Fire will confront him. So whoever among you can protect himself from the Fire even with half a date, let him do so." [[The addition in brackets is from Sahih Muslim.]]

Al-Hasan said: "When the sun is wrapped up" is an oath whose answer is "Every soul will know what it has presented," just as one says: "If Zayd sets off, Amr sets off." But the first view is more correct. Ibn Zayd narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ up to His words: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾, that there are twelve characteristics: six in this world and six in the Hereafter. And we have already explained the first six by the statement of Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 81, verses 1–14 (part 1 of 2):

The Surah al-Takwir (Surah of the Folding Up) is Meccan, according to the consensus. It has twenty-nine verses. In al-Tirmidhi, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look at the Day of Resurrection as if he saw it with his own eye, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾, and ﴿When the sky is torn apart﴾." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan [gharib]. [The addition is from the text of Sahih al-Tirmidhi.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿When the sun is wrapped up (1). And when the stars fall away (2). And when the mountains are set moving (3). And when the pregnant camels are abandoned (4). And when the wild beasts are gathered together (5). And when the seas are set ablaze (6). And when the souls are paired (7). And when the buried infant girl is asked (8) for what sin she was killed (9). And when the pages are laid open (10). And when the sky is stripped away (11). And when Hellfire is kindled (12). And when Paradise is brought near (13), a soul will know what it has presented (14).﴾

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: its folding up is its being made to enter the Throne. Al-Hasan said: it is the going away of its light. Qatadah and Mujahid said the same, and it is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it was made to lose its light ('uwwirat). Abu 'Ubaydah said: it was wrapped up like the winding of a turban, folded and effaced. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: it was wrapped up, meaning it was thrown away. From this comes the expression kawwartuhu fa-takawwara, meaning he threw it down so that it fell. I say: the root meaning of al-takwir is gathering together, derived from the phrase kara al-'imamata 'ala ra'sihi yakurruha, meaning he wrapped the turban around his head and gathered it. So it is wrapped up, its light is effaced, and then it is thrown into the sea. And Allah knows best. It is also narrated from Abu Salih that kuwwirat means it was turned upside down (nukkisat).

(﴿And when the stars fall away﴾) means they fall down and scatter. Abu 'Ubaydah said: they pour down, as the eagle pours down when it swoops. Al-'Ajjaj, describing a falcon, said:

"He saw a kharban in the open and swooped down,
like a falcon swooping when it dives."

Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On that day no star will remain in the sky without falling to the earth, until the people of the seventh earth are terrified by what has befallen them and it strikes the upper [earth]," meaning the earth. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they fell down. That is because they are lamps suspended between heaven and earth by chains of light, and those chains are in the hands of angels of light. When the First Trumpet comes, whoever is on the earth and in the heavens dies, so those stars scatter and the chains fall from the hands of the angels, because whoever was holding them has died. It is also possible that their infiltration (inkidar) means the effacing of their traces. The stars were called nujum (stars) because they appear in the sky by their light. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "inkadarat" means they changed, so that no light remained for them because they were removed from their places. The meanings are close.

(﴿And when the mountains are set moving﴾) means they are uprooted from the earth and set moving through the air. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day We set the mountains moving, you will see the earth laid bare﴾ [al-Kahf: 47]. It was also said: their movement is their change from the state of stones, so they become a heap of sand that flows (kathiban mahilan), and they become like wool (al-'ihn), and they become scattered dust (habaa'an manthuran), and they become a mirage (sarab), like a mirage that is nothing. And the earth returns to be a level plain (qa'an safsafan), in which you see no crookedness or elevation. This has already been discussed in more than one place, and praise be to Allah.

(﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾) means the pregnant she-camels that have their young in their bellies. The singular is 'ushara', or it refers to she-camels in the tenth month of pregnancy. The name remains theirs until they give birth, and even after they have given birth. It is a habit of the Arabs to call a thing by its former name even when it has passed beyond that state. A man says to his horse, when it has become a mare: "Bring my colt and bring near my colt," calling it by its earlier name. 'Antarah said:

"Do not mention my colt, nor what I have made her desire,
or your skin will become like the skin of a mangy camel."

He also said:

"I carried my colt into the midst of them, and it went on,
[after I had gored the horns of their ram, and it fell]."

The reason the pregnant camels are singled out for mention is that they are the most precious possessions to the Arabs, and their owners abandon them only in the state of the Resurrection. This is said as an example, because in the Resurrection there will be no pregnant she-camel. Rather, the intention is the example that the terror of the Day of Resurrection will be such that if a man had a pregnant she-camel he would abandon it and busy himself with himself. It was also said: when they rise from their graves and see one another, and they see the wild beasts and animals gathered together, among which are their pregnant camels, which were their most valued wealth, they will pay them no heed and their concern for them will be gone. The Arabs were addressed concerning the pregnant camels because most of their wealth and livelihood consisted of camels. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "'uttilat" means its owners left it idle because they were preoccupied with themselves. Al-A'sha said:

"He is the giver of a hundred, chosen, whether young camels in their second year or pregnant camels."

Another said:

"You see the man forsaken when his wealth dwindles,
while the rich man is visited and his company sought.
The wealth of the one who is visited does not benefit the visitors
when the she-camels of his herd graze and the pregnant camels are with him."

It is said: naqah 'ushara (a she-camel in her tenth month), and naqatan 'usharawan, and nuq 'ishar and 'usharawat, substituting a waw for the feminine hamza. And the she-camel became 'ushara, that is, she reached her tenth month. It was also said: al-'ishar is the cloud, which is left idle of what is in it, namely water, so it does not rain. The Arabs liken the cloud to a pregnant woman. It was also said: the dwellings are abandoned so that no one lives in them. It was also said: the land whose crop is taxed (yu'ashsharu) is left idle so that it is not sown. The first meaning is more well known, and most people hold it.

(﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾) means they are assembled. Al-hashr means gathering. This is narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. Ibn 'Abbas said: their gathering is their death. 'Ikrimah narrated it from him. The gathering of everything is its death, except jinn and humans, for they will be present on the Day of Resurrection. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: everything will be gathered, even the fly. Ibn 'Abbas said: the wild beasts will be gathered tomorrow, that is, they will be brought together until retribution is taken for some of them from others. Retribution will be taken for the hornless animal from the horned one, and then it will be said to them, "Be dust," and they will die. This is more sound than what 'Ikrimah narrated from him. I have explained this fully in my book al-Tadhkirah, and part of it has passed in Surah al-An'am [vol. 6, p. 421]. That is, if the wild beasts are in this state, how much more so the children of Adam. It was also said: what is meant is that although today they flee from people and wander in the deserts, tomorrow they will join people because of the terrors of that day. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said this.

(﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾) means they are filled with water. The Arabs say: sajarat al-hawd asjuruhu sajran, meaning I filled the pool. It is masjur, and al-masjur and al-sajir in the language mean full. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym narrated: "sujjirat" means it overflowed and was filled. This was said also by al-Kalbi, Muqatil, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak. Ibn Abi Zamanin said: the true meaning of sujjirat is filled, so that some of them overflow into others until they become one thing. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan. It was also said: He released its sweet water onto its brackish water and its brackish water onto its sweet water, until it was full. This is from al-Dahhak and Mujahid: that is, they were made to burst forth so that they became one sea. Al-Qushayri said: this happens when Allah removes the barrier mentioned in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾ [al-Rahman: 20]. When that barrier is lifted, the waters of the seas will gush forth and cover the whole earth, and the seas will become one sea. It was also said: they will become one sea of scalding water for the people of the Fire. It is also narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Hayyan: they will dry up so that not a drop of their water remains. Al-Qushayri said: it derives from sajartu al-tannur asjuruhu sajran, meaning I heated the oven. When the kindling is applied to it, whatever moisture is in it dries up. At that time the mountains will be set moving, and the seas and the entire earth will become one plain, by filling the place of the seas with the dust of the mountains. Al-Nahhas said: the opinions may be in agreement, so that the water dries up after it has overflowed, some of it into others, and then it turns into fire. I say: then the mountains will be set moving at that time, as al-Qushayri mentioned, and Allah knows best. Ibn Zayd, Shimr, 'Atiyyah, Sufyan, Wahb, Ubayy, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of al-Dahhak from him said: they will be kindled and become fire. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah will fold up the sun, the moon and the stars into the sea, and then Allah will send upon it a western wind, which will blow on it until it becomes fire. Similarly, in some hadith: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic is His praise, will command the sun, the moon and the stars, and they will be scattered into the sea. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is His praise, will send the west wind, which will set them ablaze, and that is the Great Fire of Allah, with which He will punish the disbelievers." Al-Qushayri said: it has been said in explaining the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, "sujjirat means were kindled," that it is possible that Hell is in the depths of the seas, and it is not kindled now for the sake of the continuation of this world. When this world ends, it will be kindled, and all of it will become fire, into which Allah will admit its people. It is also possible that beneath the sea there is fire, and then Allah will kindle the whole sea so that it becomes fire. And in a report: "The sea is fire within fire."

Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'id said: the Roman Sea is in the middle of the earth, and beneath it are sealed wells of copper, which will be kindled as fire on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the sun will be in the sea, and the sea will become fire from the heat of the sun. Then everything mentioned in these verses may occur in this world before the Day of Resurrection and be among its signs, and it may occur on the Day of Resurrection itself, and what comes after these verses will be on the Day of Resurrection. I say: it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that one should not perform ablution with sea water because it is the lid of Hell. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: there are six signs before the Day of Resurrection: while people are in their markets, the light of the sun will go away and the stars will appear, and they will be bewildered and astonished. While they are in that state, looking, the stars will scatter and fall. While they are in that state, the mountains will fall upon the face of the earth, shaking, convulsing and burning, until they become scattered dust. The people will flee to the jinn, and the jinn to the people, and the beasts, wild animals, insects and birds will mingle, and some of them will surge into others. That is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾. Then the jinn will say to the people, "We will bring you the news," so they will set off to the seas, and behold, they are a blazing fire. While they are in that state, the earth will split open in one cleft, down to the lowest seventh earth, and up to the highest seventh heaven. While they are in that state, a wind will come upon them and cause them to die. It was also said: the meaning of "sujjirat" is the redness of its water, until it becomes like blood, derived from the expression 'ayn sajra', meaning a red eye. Ibn Kathir read sujjirat, and Abu 'Amr also did, as a report about its state once. The rest read it with the doubled letter (shaddah), as a report about its state in the repetition of that happening again and again.

**Verse 1–14 (part 2 of 2)**

His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the souls are paired﴾. Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said regarding "When the souls are paired" that it means: "Each man will be joined with the people whose deeds were like his." Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The wicked will be joined with the wicked, and the righteous with the righteous. Ibn Abbas said: That is when people become three pairs: the foremost (al-sabiqun) are one pair, meaning one category; the companions of the right are one pair; and the companions of the left are one pair. He also said: The souls of the believers are paired with the wide-eyed maidens (al-hur al-'in), the disbeliever is joined with the devils, and likewise the hypocrites. He also said: Every kind is joined with its like from the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire. So the outstanding in obedience is joined with his like, the moderate with his like, and the people of disobedience with their like. Thus "tazwij" (pairing) means that a thing is joined with its like, and the meaning is: "When the souls are joined with their likes in Paradise and Hellfire." It was also said: Each man is joined with those whom he used to be bound to, such as a king or ruler, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat: 22]. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: They are made into pairs according to the similarity of their deeds, not by marriage: the companions of the right are one pair, the companions of the left are one pair, and the foremost are one pair. And He, whose praise is exalted, has said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat: 22], meaning their likes. Ikrimah said: "When the souls are paired" means the spirits are joined to the bodies, that is, returned to them. Al-Hasan said: Every person is attached to his faction: the Jews with the Jews, the Christians with the Christians, the Magians with the Magians, and everyone who worshipped anything besides Allah is joined with those like him; the hypocrites with the hypocrites, and the believers with the believers. It was also said: The one who went astray is joined with whoever misled him, whether a devil or a human, by way of hatred and enmity; and the obedient is joined with whoever called him to obedience from among the prophets and the believers. It was also said: The souls are joined with their deeds, and because of their close association with them, this is like marriage.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾. Al-mawuda is the one who is killed, namely the girl who is buried alive. She was named so because of the earth that is thrown upon her, so that it "yu'iduha," meaning weighs her down until she dies. From this is His word, exalted is He: ﴿and He is not burdened by their preservation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], meaning it does not weigh Him down. Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah said:

*A buried infant girl, interred in a desert,*
*with her afterbirth, pressed down, not prepared.*

[It is narrated thus and attributed to Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah in the原 sources; the Lisan and the Sharh al-Qamus, under the root (ʿ-w-z), attribute it to Hassan (may Allah be pleased with him), and they narrate it as:

*A buried infant girl, chilled in wraps,*
*with her afterbirth, crushed, not laid to rest.*

The "amah" is what clings to the navel of a newborn when it falls from its mother's womb. The "ma'awiz" are rags in which a child is wrapped.]

They used to bury their daughters alive for two reasons. The first: they used to say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, so they attributed daughters to Him. The second: either out of fear of poverty and destitution, or out of fear of captivity and enslavement. This meaning has been discussed fully in Surah al-Nahl [[See vol. 10, p. 117]], at His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or bury it in the dust﴾ [al-Nahl: 59]. The people of nobility among them used to refrain from this and forbid it, until al-Farazdaq boasted about it, saying:

*And from us is the one who forbade the burial of daughters,*
*so he revived the buried and they were not buried.*

[It is also narrated: "My grandfather who forbade the burial of daughters…" etc.]

He means his grandfather Sa'sa'ah, who used to buy them from their fathers. Then Islam came, and he had revived seventy buried girls. Ibn Abbas said: In the pre-Islamic era, when a woman became pregnant, she dug a pit and gave birth over it. If she bore a girl, she threw her into the pit and returned the dirt over her; and if she bore a boy, she kept him. From this is the saying of the rajiz (a rhyming verse composer):

*I named her when she was born, that she would die,*
*and the grave is a relative who guarantees, a weighty one.*

Al-zimmit means the dignified and grave; al-zamit has the pattern of al-fisiq, and is more dignified than al-zimmit. It is said: "Fulan is azmat al-nas," meaning the most dignified of them, and how intense is his solemnity. This is from al-Farra'. Qatadah said: In the pre-Islamic era, one of them would kill his daughter while feeding his dog. Allah rebuked them for that and threatened them with His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾.

Umar said concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: Qays ibn Asim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! I buried eight daughters who were mine in the pre-Islamic era." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a owner of camels." He said: "Then send a badanah (camel for sacrifice) for each one of them, if you wish."

As for His words, ﴿is asked﴾: the questioning of the buried girl is a rebuke to her killer, just as one says to a child when he is beaten: "Why were you beaten? What is your fault?" Al-Hasan said: Allah wished to rebuke her killer, because she was killed without any fault. Ibn Aslam said: "For what sin was she struck?" — for they used to strike her. Some scholars said concerning His words, ﴿is asked﴾: it means "is sought," as if he meant: just as blood is sought from the slain. He said: This is like His words: ﴿And the covenant of Allah was ever to be questioned﴾ [al-Ahzab: 15], meaning it would be demanded. So it is as if she is demanded from them, and it is said: "Where are your children?"

Al-Dahhak and Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn Zayd, recited: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾, so the girl clings to her father and says: "For what sin did you kill me?" and he has no excuse. This was said by Ibn Abbas, who used to recite it this way, and it is thus in the Mushaf of Ubayy (ibn Ka'b). Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The woman who kills her child will come on the Day of Resurrection with her child clinging to her breasts, smeared with his blood, and he will say: 'O Lord, this is my mother, and this is the one who killed me.'"

The first opinion is the view of the majority, and it is like His word to Jesus: ﴿Did you say to the people…﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116], by way of rebuke and reproach to them. Likewise, the questioning of the buried girl is a rebuke to the one who buried her. This is more emphatic than asking her about her killing, because that cannot be correct without a sin; so "for what sin was it done?" — when it becomes clear that she had no sin, it is greater in its severity and in the manifestation of the proof against her killer. And Allah knows best.

It was read "qutthilat" with shaddah (intensive), and this is clear evidence that the children of polytheists are not punished, and that punishment is not deserved except for a sin.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾: that is, they are opened after having been folded. The intended meaning is the pages of deeds, in which the angels wrote what its people did of good and evil. They are folded by death and unfolded on the Day of Resurrection, and each person stands before his page and knows what is in it, and says: ﴿What is this book that leaves out nothing small or great, except that it has counted it?﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. Marthad ibn Wada'ah narrated: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the pages will fly from beneath the Throne. The page of the believer will fall into his hand in a lofty Garden [al-Haqqah: 22], up to His words: ﴿the days gone by﴾ [al-Haqqah: 24]; and the page of the disbeliever will fall into his hand in scorching wind and boiling water, up to His words: ﴿nor generous﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 42–44]. It is narrated from Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot and naked." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the women?" He said: "People will be preoccupied, O Umm Salamah." I said: "And what will preoccupy them?" He said: "The unfolding of the pages, in which are the weights of atoms and the weights of mustard seeds."

It has already passed in Surah al-Isra [[See vol. 10, p. 230]] the saying of Abu al-Thawwar al-Adawi: "There are two unfoldings and one folding. As for what you live, O son of Adam, your page is open, so hope in it as you wish. When you die, it is folded; then when you are raised, it is unfolded: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra: 14]." Muqatil said: When a person dies, the page of his deeds is folded; when the Day of Resurrection comes, it is unfolded. It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that when he read it, he would say: "To You the matter is driven, O son of Adam."

Nafi', Ibn Amir, Asim and Abu Amr read "nushirat" with the light form (takhfif), meaning it was unfolded once, for the establishment of the proof. The rest read it with the shaddah (tashdid), meaning repeated unfolding, for emphasis in rebuking the disobedient and giving glad tidings to the obedient. It was also said: it is for the repetition of this by the human being and by the angels who bear witness against him.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾. Al-kashṭ means pulling off with great adhesion. So the sky is stripped away as the hide is stripped from a ram or other animal. Al-qashṭ is a dialectal form of it. In Abdullah's reading: "And when the sky is stripped." I stripped the camel's hide (kashṭan): I removed its skin. It is not said "salakhtuh" (I flayed it), because the Arabs say about the camel only "kashaṭtuhu" or "jaladtuhu." "Inkashaṭa" means it went away. So the sky is pulled from its place as a covering is pulled from a thing. It was also said: it is folded, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the day We fold up the sky like the folding of the scroll for the books﴾ [al-Anbiya: 104]. So the meaning is: it is uprooted and then folded. And Allah knows best.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Hellfire is set ablaze﴾: that is, it is kindled and set aflame for the disbelievers, and its heat is increased. It is said: "sa''altu al-nar" and "asta'altuha" (I kindled the fire). The reading of the majority is with the light form, from "al-sa'ir" (the blaze). Nafi', Ibn Dhakwan and Ruways read it with the shaddah, because it was kindled repeatedly, time after time. Qatadah said: Its kindling was caused by the anger of Allah and the sins of the children of Adam. In al-Tirmidhi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The Fire was kindled for a thousand years until it became red, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became white, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became black; so it is black and dark." It is also narrated as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: that is, it draws near and comes close to the God-fearing. Al-Hasan said: They will be brought close to it, not that it will move from its place. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd used to say: "It was adorned…"[[In Z: "it was brought near."]] — "uzlifat?" And "al-zulfa" in the language of the Arabs is nearness, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 90]. And "tazallafa fulan" means he drew near.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Every soul will know what it has presented﴾, meaning what it did of good and evil. This is the answer to "When the sun is wrapped up" and what follows it. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: For this the narration was ordered. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that they recited it, and when they reached "Every soul will know what it has presented," they said: "For this the narrative was arranged." So the meaning according to this is: "When the sun is wrapped up," and these things happen, "every soul will know what it has presented of its deeds." In the two Sahihs, from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is none among you but Allah will speak to him, with no interpreter between them. He will look to his right and see nothing but what he has sent forth, and he will look to his left and see nothing but what he has sent forth [and he will look to his left and see nothing but what he has sent forth]. Then the Fire will confront him. So whoever among you can protect himself from the Fire even with half a date, let him do so." [[The addition in brackets is from Sahih Muslim.]]

Al-Hasan said: "When the sun is wrapped up" is an oath whose answer is "Every soul will know what it has presented," just as one says: "If Zayd sets off, Amr sets off." But the first view is more correct. Ibn Zayd narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ up to His words: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾, that there are twelve characteristics: six in this world and six in the Hereafter. And we have already explained the first six by the statement of Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 81, verses 1–14 (part 1 of 2):

The Surah al-Takwir (Surah of the Folding Up) is Meccan, according to the consensus. It has twenty-nine verses. In al-Tirmidhi, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look at the Day of Resurrection as if he saw it with his own eye, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾, and ﴿When the sky is torn apart﴾." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan [gharib]. [The addition is from the text of Sahih al-Tirmidhi.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿When the sun is wrapped up (1). And when the stars fall away (2). And when the mountains are set moving (3). And when the pregnant camels are abandoned (4). And when the wild beasts are gathered together (5). And when the seas are set ablaze (6). And when the souls are paired (7). And when the buried infant girl is asked (8) for what sin she was killed (9). And when the pages are laid open (10). And when the sky is stripped away (11). And when Hellfire is kindled (12). And when Paradise is brought near (13), a soul will know what it has presented (14).﴾

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: its folding up is its being made to enter the Throne. Al-Hasan said: it is the going away of its light. Qatadah and Mujahid said the same, and it is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it was made to lose its light ('uwwirat). Abu 'Ubaydah said: it was wrapped up like the winding of a turban, folded and effaced. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: it was wrapped up, meaning it was thrown away. From this comes the expression kawwartuhu fa-takawwara, meaning he threw it down so that it fell. I say: the root meaning of al-takwir is gathering together, derived from the phrase kara al-'imamata 'ala ra'sihi yakurruha, meaning he wrapped the turban around his head and gathered it. So it is wrapped up, its light is effaced, and then it is thrown into the sea. And Allah knows best. It is also narrated from Abu Salih that kuwwirat means it was turned upside down (nukkisat).

(﴿And when the stars fall away﴾) means they fall down and scatter. Abu 'Ubaydah said: they pour down, as the eagle pours down when it swoops. Al-'Ajjaj, describing a falcon, said:

"He saw a kharban in the open and swooped down,
like a falcon swooping when it dives."

Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On that day no star will remain in the sky without falling to the earth, until the people of the seventh earth are terrified by what has befallen them and it strikes the upper [earth]," meaning the earth. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they fell down. That is because they are lamps suspended between heaven and earth by chains of light, and those chains are in the hands of angels of light. When the First Trumpet comes, whoever is on the earth and in the heavens dies, so those stars scatter and the chains fall from the hands of the angels, because whoever was holding them has died. It is also possible that their infiltration (inkidar) means the effacing of their traces. The stars were called nujum (stars) because they appear in the sky by their light. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "inkadarat" means they changed, so that no light remained for them because they were removed from their places. The meanings are close.

(﴿And when the mountains are set moving﴾) means they are uprooted from the earth and set moving through the air. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day We set the mountains moving, you will see the earth laid bare﴾ [al-Kahf: 47]. It was also said: their movement is their change from the state of stones, so they become a heap of sand that flows (kathiban mahilan), and they become like wool (al-'ihn), and they become scattered dust (habaa'an manthuran), and they become a mirage (sarab), like a mirage that is nothing. And the earth returns to be a level plain (qa'an safsafan), in which you see no crookedness or elevation. This has already been discussed in more than one place, and praise be to Allah.

(﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾) means the pregnant she-camels that have their young in their bellies. The singular is 'ushara', or it refers to she-camels in the tenth month of pregnancy. The name remains theirs until they give birth, and even after they have given birth. It is a habit of the Arabs to call a thing by its former name even when it has passed beyond that state. A man says to his horse, when it has become a mare: "Bring my colt and bring near my colt," calling it by its earlier name. 'Antarah said:

"Do not mention my colt, nor what I have made her desire,
or your skin will become like the skin of a mangy camel."

He also said:

"I carried my colt into the midst of them, and it went on,
[after I had gored the horns of their ram, and it fell]."

The reason the pregnant camels are singled out for mention is that they are the most precious possessions to the Arabs, and their owners abandon them only in the state of the Resurrection. This is said as an example, because in the Resurrection there will be no pregnant she-camel. Rather, the intention is the example that the terror of the Day of Resurrection will be such that if a man had a pregnant she-camel he would abandon it and busy himself with himself. It was also said: when they rise from their graves and see one another, and they see the wild beasts and animals gathered together, among which are their pregnant camels, which were their most valued wealth, they will pay them no heed and their concern for them will be gone. The Arabs were addressed concerning the pregnant camels because most of their wealth and livelihood consisted of camels. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "'uttilat" means its owners left it idle because they were preoccupied with themselves. Al-A'sha said:

"He is the giver of a hundred, chosen, whether young camels in their second year or pregnant camels."

Another said:

"You see the man forsaken when his wealth dwindles,
while the rich man is visited and his company sought.
The wealth of the one who is visited does not benefit the visitors
when the she-camels of his herd graze and the pregnant camels are with him."

It is said: naqah 'ushara (a she-camel in her tenth month), and naqatan 'usharawan, and nuq 'ishar and 'usharawat, substituting a waw for the feminine hamza. And the she-camel became 'ushara, that is, she reached her tenth month. It was also said: al-'ishar is the cloud, which is left idle of what is in it, namely water, so it does not rain. The Arabs liken the cloud to a pregnant woman. It was also said: the dwellings are abandoned so that no one lives in them. It was also said: the land whose crop is taxed (yu'ashsharu) is left idle so that it is not sown. The first meaning is more well known, and most people hold it.

(﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾) means they are assembled. Al-hashr means gathering. This is narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. Ibn 'Abbas said: their gathering is their death. 'Ikrimah narrated it from him. The gathering of everything is its death, except jinn and humans, for they will be present on the Day of Resurrection. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: everything will be gathered, even the fly. Ibn 'Abbas said: the wild beasts will be gathered tomorrow, that is, they will be brought together until retribution is taken for some of them from others. Retribution will be taken for the hornless animal from the horned one, and then it will be said to them, "Be dust," and they will die. This is more sound than what 'Ikrimah narrated from him. I have explained this fully in my book al-Tadhkirah, and part of it has passed in Surah al-An'am [vol. 6, p. 421]. That is, if the wild beasts are in this state, how much more so the children of Adam. It was also said: what is meant is that although today they flee from people and wander in the deserts, tomorrow they will join people because of the terrors of that day. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said this.

(﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾) means they are filled with water. The Arabs say: sajarat al-hawd asjuruhu sajran, meaning I filled the pool. It is masjur, and al-masjur and al-sajir in the language mean full. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym narrated: "sujjirat" means it overflowed and was filled. This was said also by al-Kalbi, Muqatil, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak. Ibn Abi Zamanin said: the true meaning of sujjirat is filled, so that some of them overflow into others until they become one thing. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan. It was also said: He released its sweet water onto its brackish water and its brackish water onto its sweet water, until it was full. This is from al-Dahhak and Mujahid: that is, they were made to burst forth so that they became one sea. Al-Qushayri said: this happens when Allah removes the barrier mentioned in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾ [al-Rahman: 20]. When that barrier is lifted, the waters of the seas will gush forth and cover the whole earth, and the seas will become one sea. It was also said: they will become one sea of scalding water for the people of the Fire. It is also narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Hayyan: they will dry up so that not a drop of their water remains. Al-Qushayri said: it derives from sajartu al-tannur asjuruhu sajran, meaning I heated the oven. When the kindling is applied to it, whatever moisture is in it dries up. At that time the mountains will be set moving, and the seas and the entire earth will become one plain, by filling the place of the seas with the dust of the mountains. Al-Nahhas said: the opinions may be in agreement, so that the water dries up after it has overflowed, some of it into others, and then it turns into fire. I say: then the mountains will be set moving at that time, as al-Qushayri mentioned, and Allah knows best. Ibn Zayd, Shimr, 'Atiyyah, Sufyan, Wahb, Ubayy, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of al-Dahhak from him said: they will be kindled and become fire. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah will fold up the sun, the moon and the stars into the sea, and then Allah will send upon it a western wind, which will blow on it until it becomes fire. Similarly, in some hadith: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic is His praise, will command the sun, the moon and the stars, and they will be scattered into the sea. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is His praise, will send the west wind, which will set them ablaze, and that is the Great Fire of Allah, with which He will punish the disbelievers." Al-Qushayri said: it has been said in explaining the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, "sujjirat means were kindled," that it is possible that Hell is in the depths of the seas, and it is not kindled now for the sake of the continuation of this world. When this world ends, it will be kindled, and all of it will become fire, into which Allah will admit its people. It is also possible that beneath the sea there is fire, and then Allah will kindle the whole sea so that it becomes fire. And in a report: "The sea is fire within fire."

Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'id said: the Roman Sea is in the middle of the earth, and beneath it are sealed wells of copper, which will be kindled as fire on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the sun will be in the sea, and the sea will become fire from the heat of the sun. Then everything mentioned in these verses may occur in this world before the Day of Resurrection and be among its signs, and it may occur on the Day of Resurrection itself, and what comes after these verses will be on the Day of Resurrection. I say: it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that one should not perform ablution with sea water because it is the lid of Hell. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: there are six signs before the Day of Resurrection: while people are in their markets, the light of the sun will go away and the stars will appear, and they will be bewildered and astonished. While they are in that state, looking, the stars will scatter and fall. While they are in that state, the mountains will fall upon the face of the earth, shaking, convulsing and burning, until they become scattered dust. The people will flee to the jinn, and the jinn to the people, and the beasts, wild animals, insects and birds will mingle, and some of them will surge into others. That is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾. Then the jinn will say to the people, "We will bring you the news," so they will set off to the seas, and behold, they are a blazing fire. While they are in that state, the earth will split open in one cleft, down to the lowest seventh earth, and up to the highest seventh heaven. While they are in that state, a wind will come upon them and cause them to die. It was also said: the meaning of "sujjirat" is the redness of its water, until it becomes like blood, derived from the expression 'ayn sajra', meaning a red eye. Ibn Kathir read sujjirat, and Abu 'Amr also did, as a report about its state once. The rest read it with the doubled letter (shaddah), as a report about its state in the repetition of that happening again and again.

**Verse 1–14 (part 2 of 2)**

His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the souls are paired﴾. Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said regarding "When the souls are paired" that it means: "Each man will be joined with the people whose deeds were like his." Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The wicked will be joined with the wicked, and the righteous with the righteous. Ibn Abbas said: That is when people become three pairs: the foremost (al-sabiqun) are one pair, meaning one category; the companions of the right are one pair; and the companions of the left are one pair. He also said: The souls of the believers are paired with the wide-eyed maidens (al-hur al-'in), the disbeliever is joined with the devils, and likewise the hypocrites. He also said: Every kind is joined with its like from the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire. So the outstanding in obedience is joined with his like, the moderate with his like, and the people of disobedience with their like. Thus "tazwij" (pairing) means that a thing is joined with its like, and the meaning is: "When the souls are joined with their likes in Paradise and Hellfire." It was also said: Each man is joined with those whom he used to be bound to, such as a king or ruler, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat: 22]. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: They are made into pairs according to the similarity of their deeds, not by marriage: the companions of the right are one pair, the companions of the left are one pair, and the foremost are one pair. And He, whose praise is exalted, has said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat: 22], meaning their likes. Ikrimah said: "When the souls are paired" means the spirits are joined to the bodies, that is, returned to them. Al-Hasan said: Every person is attached to his faction: the Jews with the Jews, the Christians with the Christians, the Magians with the Magians, and everyone who worshipped anything besides Allah is joined with those like him; the hypocrites with the hypocrites, and the believers with the believers. It was also said: The one who went astray is joined with whoever misled him, whether a devil or a human, by way of hatred and enmity; and the obedient is joined with whoever called him to obedience from among the prophets and the believers. It was also said: The souls are joined with their deeds, and because of their close association with them, this is like marriage.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾. Al-mawuda is the one who is killed, namely the girl who is buried alive. She was named so because of the earth that is thrown upon her, so that it "yu'iduha," meaning weighs her down until she dies. From this is His word, exalted is He: ﴿and He is not burdened by their preservation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], meaning it does not weigh Him down. Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah said:

*A buried infant girl, interred in a desert,*
*with her afterbirth, pressed down, not prepared.*

[It is narrated thus and attributed to Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah in the原 sources; the Lisan and the Sharh al-Qamus, under the root (ʿ-w-z), attribute it to Hassan (may Allah be pleased with him), and they narrate it as:

*A buried infant girl, chilled in wraps,*
*with her afterbirth, crushed, not laid to rest.*

The "amah" is what clings to the navel of a newborn when it falls from its mother's womb. The "ma'awiz" are rags in which a child is wrapped.]

They used to bury their daughters alive for two reasons. The first: they used to say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, so they attributed daughters to Him. The second: either out of fear of poverty and destitution, or out of fear of captivity and enslavement. This meaning has been discussed fully in Surah al-Nahl [[See vol. 10, p. 117]], at His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or bury it in the dust﴾ [al-Nahl: 59]. The people of nobility among them used to refrain from this and forbid it, until al-Farazdaq boasted about it, saying:

*And from us is the one who forbade the burial of daughters,*
*so he revived the buried and they were not buried.*

[It is also narrated: "My grandfather who forbade the burial of daughters…" etc.]

He means his grandfather Sa'sa'ah, who used to buy them from their fathers. Then Islam came, and he had revived seventy buried girls. Ibn Abbas said: In the pre-Islamic era, when a woman became pregnant, she dug a pit and gave birth over it. If she bore a girl, she threw her into the pit and returned the dirt over her; and if she bore a boy, she kept him. From this is the saying of the rajiz (a rhyming verse composer):

*I named her when she was born, that she would die,*
*and the grave is a relative who guarantees, a weighty one.*

Al-zimmit means the dignified and grave; al-zamit has the pattern of al-fisiq, and is more dignified than al-zimmit. It is said: "Fulan is azmat al-nas," meaning the most dignified of them, and how intense is his solemnity. This is from al-Farra'. Qatadah said: In the pre-Islamic era, one of them would kill his daughter while feeding his dog. Allah rebuked them for that and threatened them with His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾.

Umar said concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: Qays ibn Asim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! I buried eight daughters who were mine in the pre-Islamic era." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a owner of camels." He said: "Then send a badanah (camel for sacrifice) for each one of them, if you wish."

As for His words, ﴿is asked﴾: the questioning of the buried girl is a rebuke to her killer, just as one says to a child when he is beaten: "Why were you beaten? What is your fault?" Al-Hasan said: Allah wished to rebuke her killer, because she was killed without any fault. Ibn Aslam said: "For what sin was she struck?" — for they used to strike her. Some scholars said concerning His words, ﴿is asked﴾: it means "is sought," as if he meant: just as blood is sought from the slain. He said: This is like His words: ﴿And the covenant of Allah was ever to be questioned﴾ [al-Ahzab: 15], meaning it would be demanded. So it is as if she is demanded from them, and it is said: "Where are your children?"

Al-Dahhak and Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn Zayd, recited: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾, so the girl clings to her father and says: "For what sin did you kill me?" and he has no excuse. This was said by Ibn Abbas, who used to recite it this way, and it is thus in the Mushaf of Ubayy (ibn Ka'b). Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The woman who kills her child will come on the Day of Resurrection with her child clinging to her breasts, smeared with his blood, and he will say: 'O Lord, this is my mother, and this is the one who killed me.'"

The first opinion is the view of the majority, and it is like His word to Jesus: ﴿Did you say to the people…﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116], by way of rebuke and reproach to them. Likewise, the questioning of the buried girl is a rebuke to the one who buried her. This is more emphatic than asking her about her killing, because that cannot be correct without a sin; so "for what sin was it done?" — when it becomes clear that she had no sin, it is greater in its severity and in the manifestation of the proof against her killer. And Allah knows best.

It was read "qutthilat" with shaddah (intensive), and this is clear evidence that the children of polytheists are not punished, and that punishment is not deserved except for a sin.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾: that is, they are opened after having been folded. The intended meaning is the pages of deeds, in which the angels wrote what its people did of good and evil. They are folded by death and unfolded on the Day of Resurrection, and each person stands before his page and knows what is in it, and says: ﴿What is this book that leaves out nothing small or great, except that it has counted it?﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. Marthad ibn Wada'ah narrated: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the pages will fly from beneath the Throne. The page of the believer will fall into his hand in a lofty Garden [al-Haqqah: 22], up to His words: ﴿the days gone by﴾ [al-Haqqah: 24]; and the page of the disbeliever will fall into his hand in scorching wind and boiling water, up to His words: ﴿nor generous﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 42–44]. It is narrated from Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot and naked." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the women?" He said: "People will be preoccupied, O Umm Salamah." I said: "And what will preoccupy them?" He said: "The unfolding of the pages, in which are the weights of atoms and the weights of mustard seeds."

It has already passed in Surah al-Isra [[See vol. 10, p. 230]] the saying of Abu al-Thawwar al-Adawi: "There are two unfoldings and one folding. As for what you live, O son of Adam, your page is open, so hope in it as you wish. When you die, it is folded; then when you are raised, it is unfolded: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra: 14]." Muqatil said: When a person dies, the page of his deeds is folded; when the Day of Resurrection comes, it is unfolded. It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that when he read it, he would say: "To You the matter is driven, O son of Adam."

Nafi', Ibn Amir, Asim and Abu Amr read "nushirat" with the light form (takhfif), meaning it was unfolded once, for the establishment of the proof. The rest read it with the shaddah (tashdid), meaning repeated unfolding, for emphasis in rebuking the disobedient and giving glad tidings to the obedient. It was also said: it is for the repetition of this by the human being and by the angels who bear witness against him.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾. Al-kashṭ means pulling off with great adhesion. So the sky is stripped away as the hide is stripped from a ram or other animal. Al-qashṭ is a dialectal form of it. In Abdullah's reading: "And when the sky is stripped." I stripped the camel's hide (kashṭan): I removed its skin. It is not said "salakhtuh" (I flayed it), because the Arabs say about the camel only "kashaṭtuhu" or "jaladtuhu." "Inkashaṭa" means it went away. So the sky is pulled from its place as a covering is pulled from a thing. It was also said: it is folded, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the day We fold up the sky like the folding of the scroll for the books﴾ [al-Anbiya: 104]. So the meaning is: it is uprooted and then folded. And Allah knows best.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Hellfire is set ablaze﴾: that is, it is kindled and set aflame for the disbelievers, and its heat is increased. It is said: "sa''altu al-nar" and "asta'altuha" (I kindled the fire). The reading of the majority is with the light form, from "al-sa'ir" (the blaze). Nafi', Ibn Dhakwan and Ruways read it with the shaddah, because it was kindled repeatedly, time after time. Qatadah said: Its kindling was caused by the anger of Allah and the sins of the children of Adam. In al-Tirmidhi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The Fire was kindled for a thousand years until it became red, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became white, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became black; so it is black and dark." It is also narrated as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: that is, it draws near and comes close to the God-fearing. Al-Hasan said: They will be brought close to it, not that it will move from its place. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd used to say: "It was adorned…"[[In Z: "it was brought near."]] — "uzlifat?" And "al-zulfa" in the language of the Arabs is nearness, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 90]. And "tazallafa fulan" means he drew near.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Every soul will know what it has presented﴾, meaning what it did of good and evil. This is the answer to "When the sun is wrapped up" and what follows it. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: For this the narration was ordered. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that they recited it, and when they reached "Every soul will know what it has presented," they said: "For this the narrative was arranged." So the meaning according to this is: "When the sun is wrapped up," and these things happen, "every soul will know what it has presented of its deeds." In the two Sahihs, from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is none among you but Allah will speak to him, with no interpreter between them. He will look to his right and see nothing but what he has sent forth, and he will look to his left and see nothing but what he has sent forth [and he will look to his left and see nothing but what he has sent forth]. Then the Fire will confront him. So whoever among you can protect himself from the Fire even with half a date, let him do so." [[The addition in brackets is from Sahih Muslim.]]

Al-Hasan said: "When the sun is wrapped up" is an oath whose answer is "Every soul will know what it has presented," just as one says: "If Zayd sets off, Amr sets off." But the first view is more correct. Ibn Zayd narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ up to His words: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾, that there are twelve characteristics: six in this world and six in the Hereafter. And we have already explained the first six by the statement of Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 81, verses 1–14 (part 1 of 2):

The Surah al-Takwir (Surah of the Folding Up) is Meccan, according to the consensus. It has twenty-nine verses. In al-Tirmidhi, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look at the Day of Resurrection as if he saw it with his own eye, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾, and ﴿When the sky is torn apart﴾." He said: This is a hadith that is hasan [gharib]. [The addition is from the text of Sahih al-Tirmidhi.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿When the sun is wrapped up (1). And when the stars fall away (2). And when the mountains are set moving (3). And when the pregnant camels are abandoned (4). And when the wild beasts are gathered together (5). And when the seas are set ablaze (6). And when the souls are paired (7). And when the buried infant girl is asked (8) for what sin she was killed (9). And when the pages are laid open (10). And when the sky is stripped away (11). And when Hellfire is kindled (12). And when Paradise is brought near (13), a soul will know what it has presented (14).﴾

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: its folding up is its being made to enter the Throne. Al-Hasan said: it is the going away of its light. Qatadah and Mujahid said the same, and it is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it was made to lose its light ('uwwirat). Abu 'Ubaydah said: it was wrapped up like the winding of a turban, folded and effaced. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: it was wrapped up, meaning it was thrown away. From this comes the expression kawwartuhu fa-takawwara, meaning he threw it down so that it fell. I say: the root meaning of al-takwir is gathering together, derived from the phrase kara al-'imamata 'ala ra'sihi yakurruha, meaning he wrapped the turban around his head and gathered it. So it is wrapped up, its light is effaced, and then it is thrown into the sea. And Allah knows best. It is also narrated from Abu Salih that kuwwirat means it was turned upside down (nukkisat).

(﴿And when the stars fall away﴾) means they fall down and scatter. Abu 'Ubaydah said: they pour down, as the eagle pours down when it swoops. Al-'Ajjaj, describing a falcon, said:

"He saw a kharban in the open and swooped down,
like a falcon swooping when it dives."

Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On that day no star will remain in the sky without falling to the earth, until the people of the seventh earth are terrified by what has befallen them and it strikes the upper [earth]," meaning the earth. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they fell down. That is because they are lamps suspended between heaven and earth by chains of light, and those chains are in the hands of angels of light. When the First Trumpet comes, whoever is on the earth and in the heavens dies, so those stars scatter and the chains fall from the hands of the angels, because whoever was holding them has died. It is also possible that their infiltration (inkidar) means the effacing of their traces. The stars were called nujum (stars) because they appear in the sky by their light. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "inkadarat" means they changed, so that no light remained for them because they were removed from their places. The meanings are close.

(﴿And when the mountains are set moving﴾) means they are uprooted from the earth and set moving through the air. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day We set the mountains moving, you will see the earth laid bare﴾ [al-Kahf: 47]. It was also said: their movement is their change from the state of stones, so they become a heap of sand that flows (kathiban mahilan), and they become like wool (al-'ihn), and they become scattered dust (habaa'an manthuran), and they become a mirage (sarab), like a mirage that is nothing. And the earth returns to be a level plain (qa'an safsafan), in which you see no crookedness or elevation. This has already been discussed in more than one place, and praise be to Allah.

(﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾) means the pregnant she-camels that have their young in their bellies. The singular is 'ushara', or it refers to she-camels in the tenth month of pregnancy. The name remains theirs until they give birth, and even after they have given birth. It is a habit of the Arabs to call a thing by its former name even when it has passed beyond that state. A man says to his horse, when it has become a mare: "Bring my colt and bring near my colt," calling it by its earlier name. 'Antarah said:

"Do not mention my colt, nor what I have made her desire,
or your skin will become like the skin of a mangy camel."

He also said:

"I carried my colt into the midst of them, and it went on,
[after I had gored the horns of their ram, and it fell]."

The reason the pregnant camels are singled out for mention is that they are the most precious possessions to the Arabs, and their owners abandon them only in the state of the Resurrection. This is said as an example, because in the Resurrection there will be no pregnant she-camel. Rather, the intention is the example that the terror of the Day of Resurrection will be such that if a man had a pregnant she-camel he would abandon it and busy himself with himself. It was also said: when they rise from their graves and see one another, and they see the wild beasts and animals gathered together, among which are their pregnant camels, which were their most valued wealth, they will pay them no heed and their concern for them will be gone. The Arabs were addressed concerning the pregnant camels because most of their wealth and livelihood consisted of camels. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "'uttilat" means its owners left it idle because they were preoccupied with themselves. Al-A'sha said:

"He is the giver of a hundred, chosen, whether young camels in their second year or pregnant camels."

Another said:

"You see the man forsaken when his wealth dwindles,
while the rich man is visited and his company sought.
The wealth of the one who is visited does not benefit the visitors
when the she-camels of his herd graze and the pregnant camels are with him."

It is said: naqah 'ushara (a she-camel in her tenth month), and naqatan 'usharawan, and nuq 'ishar and 'usharawat, substituting a waw for the feminine hamza. And the she-camel became 'ushara, that is, she reached her tenth month. It was also said: al-'ishar is the cloud, which is left idle of what is in it, namely water, so it does not rain. The Arabs liken the cloud to a pregnant woman. It was also said: the dwellings are abandoned so that no one lives in them. It was also said: the land whose crop is taxed (yu'ashsharu) is left idle so that it is not sown. The first meaning is more well known, and most people hold it.

(﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾) means they are assembled. Al-hashr means gathering. This is narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. Ibn 'Abbas said: their gathering is their death. 'Ikrimah narrated it from him. The gathering of everything is its death, except jinn and humans, for they will be present on the Day of Resurrection. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: everything will be gathered, even the fly. Ibn 'Abbas said: the wild beasts will be gathered tomorrow, that is, they will be brought together until retribution is taken for some of them from others. Retribution will be taken for the hornless animal from the horned one, and then it will be said to them, "Be dust," and they will die. This is more sound than what 'Ikrimah narrated from him. I have explained this fully in my book al-Tadhkirah, and part of it has passed in Surah al-An'am [vol. 6, p. 421]. That is, if the wild beasts are in this state, how much more so the children of Adam. It was also said: what is meant is that although today they flee from people and wander in the deserts, tomorrow they will join people because of the terrors of that day. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said this.

(﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾) means they are filled with water. The Arabs say: sajarat al-hawd asjuruhu sajran, meaning I filled the pool. It is masjur, and al-masjur and al-sajir in the language mean full. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym narrated: "sujjirat" means it overflowed and was filled. This was said also by al-Kalbi, Muqatil, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak. Ibn Abi Zamanin said: the true meaning of sujjirat is filled, so that some of them overflow into others until they become one thing. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan. It was also said: He released its sweet water onto its brackish water and its brackish water onto its sweet water, until it was full. This is from al-Dahhak and Mujahid: that is, they were made to burst forth so that they became one sea. Al-Qushayri said: this happens when Allah removes the barrier mentioned in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾ [al-Rahman: 20]. When that barrier is lifted, the waters of the seas will gush forth and cover the whole earth, and the seas will become one sea. It was also said: they will become one sea of scalding water for the people of the Fire. It is also narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Hayyan: they will dry up so that not a drop of their water remains. Al-Qushayri said: it derives from sajartu al-tannur asjuruhu sajran, meaning I heated the oven. When the kindling is applied to it, whatever moisture is in it dries up. At that time the mountains will be set moving, and the seas and the entire earth will become one plain, by filling the place of the seas with the dust of the mountains. Al-Nahhas said: the opinions may be in agreement, so that the water dries up after it has overflowed, some of it into others, and then it turns into fire. I say: then the mountains will be set moving at that time, as al-Qushayri mentioned, and Allah knows best. Ibn Zayd, Shimr, 'Atiyyah, Sufyan, Wahb, Ubayy, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of al-Dahhak from him said: they will be kindled and become fire. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah will fold up the sun, the moon and the stars into the sea, and then Allah will send upon it a western wind, which will blow on it until it becomes fire. Similarly, in some hadith: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic is His praise, will command the sun, the moon and the stars, and they will be scattered into the sea. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is His praise, will send the west wind, which will set them ablaze, and that is the Great Fire of Allah, with which He will punish the disbelievers." Al-Qushayri said: it has been said in explaining the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, "sujjirat means were kindled," that it is possible that Hell is in the depths of the seas, and it is not kindled now for the sake of the continuation of this world. When this world ends, it will be kindled, and all of it will become fire, into which Allah will admit its people. It is also possible that beneath the sea there is fire, and then Allah will kindle the whole sea so that it becomes fire. And in a report: "The sea is fire within fire."

Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'id said: the Roman Sea is in the middle of the earth, and beneath it are sealed wells of copper, which will be kindled as fire on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the sun will be in the sea, and the sea will become fire from the heat of the sun. Then everything mentioned in these verses may occur in this world before the Day of Resurrection and be among its signs, and it may occur on the Day of Resurrection itself, and what comes after these verses will be on the Day of Resurrection. I say: it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that one should not perform ablution with sea water because it is the lid of Hell. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: there are six signs before the Day of Resurrection: while people are in their markets, the light of the sun will go away and the stars will appear, and they will be bewildered and astonished. While they are in that state, looking, the stars will scatter and fall. While they are in that state, the mountains will fall upon the face of the earth, shaking, convulsing and burning, until they become scattered dust. The people will flee to the jinn, and the jinn to the people, and the beasts, wild animals, insects and birds will mingle, and some of them will surge into others. That is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾. Then the jinn will say to the people, "We will bring you the news," so they will set off to the seas, and behold, they are a blazing fire. While they are in that state, the earth will split open in one cleft, down to the lowest seventh earth, and up to the highest seventh heaven. While they are in that state, a wind will come upon them and cause them to die. It was also said: the meaning of "sujjirat" is the redness of its water, until it becomes like blood, derived from the expression 'ayn sajra', meaning a red eye. Ibn Kathir read sujjirat, and Abu 'Amr also did, as a report about its state once. The rest read it with the doubled letter (shaddah), as a report about its state in the repetition of that happening again and again.

**Verse 1–14 (part 2 of 2)**

His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the souls are paired﴾. Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said regarding "When the souls are paired" that it means: "Each man will be joined with the people whose deeds were like his." Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The wicked will be joined with the wicked, and the righteous with the righteous. Ibn Abbas said: That is when people become three pairs: the foremost (al-sabiqun) are one pair, meaning one category; the companions of the right are one pair; and the companions of the left are one pair. He also said: The souls of the believers are paired with the wide-eyed maidens (al-hur al-'in), the disbeliever is joined with the devils, and likewise the hypocrites. He also said: Every kind is joined with its like from the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire. So the outstanding in obedience is joined with his like, the moderate with his like, and the people of disobedience with their like. Thus "tazwij" (pairing) means that a thing is joined with its like, and the meaning is: "When the souls are joined with their likes in Paradise and Hellfire." It was also said: Each man is joined with those whom he used to be bound to, such as a king or ruler, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat: 22]. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: They are made into pairs according to the similarity of their deeds, not by marriage: the companions of the right are one pair, the companions of the left are one pair, and the foremost are one pair. And He, whose praise is exalted, has said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat: 22], meaning their likes. Ikrimah said: "When the souls are paired" means the spirits are joined to the bodies, that is, returned to them. Al-Hasan said: Every person is attached to his faction: the Jews with the Jews, the Christians with the Christians, the Magians with the Magians, and everyone who worshipped anything besides Allah is joined with those like him; the hypocrites with the hypocrites, and the believers with the believers. It was also said: The one who went astray is joined with whoever misled him, whether a devil or a human, by way of hatred and enmity; and the obedient is joined with whoever called him to obedience from among the prophets and the believers. It was also said: The souls are joined with their deeds, and because of their close association with them, this is like marriage.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾. Al-mawuda is the one who is killed, namely the girl who is buried alive. She was named so because of the earth that is thrown upon her, so that it "yu'iduha," meaning weighs her down until she dies. From this is His word, exalted is He: ﴿and He is not burdened by their preservation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], meaning it does not weigh Him down. Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah said:

*A buried infant girl, interred in a desert,*
*with her afterbirth, pressed down, not prepared.*

[It is narrated thus and attributed to Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah in the原 sources; the Lisan and the Sharh al-Qamus, under the root (ʿ-w-z), attribute it to Hassan (may Allah be pleased with him), and they narrate it as:

*A buried infant girl, chilled in wraps,*
*with her afterbirth, crushed, not laid to rest.*

The "amah" is what clings to the navel of a newborn when it falls from its mother's womb. The "ma'awiz" are rags in which a child is wrapped.]

They used to bury their daughters alive for two reasons. The first: they used to say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, so they attributed daughters to Him. The second: either out of fear of poverty and destitution, or out of fear of captivity and enslavement. This meaning has been discussed fully in Surah al-Nahl [[See vol. 10, p. 117]], at His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or bury it in the dust﴾ [al-Nahl: 59]. The people of nobility among them used to refrain from this and forbid it, until al-Farazdaq boasted about it, saying:

*And from us is the one who forbade the burial of daughters,*
*so he revived the buried and they were not buried.*

[It is also narrated: "My grandfather who forbade the burial of daughters…" etc.]

He means his grandfather Sa'sa'ah, who used to buy them from their fathers. Then Islam came, and he had revived seventy buried girls. Ibn Abbas said: In the pre-Islamic era, when a woman became pregnant, she dug a pit and gave birth over it. If she bore a girl, she threw her into the pit and returned the dirt over her; and if she bore a boy, she kept him. From this is the saying of the rajiz (a rhyming verse composer):

*I named her when she was born, that she would die,*
*and the grave is a relative who guarantees, a weighty one.*

Al-zimmit means the dignified and grave; al-zamit has the pattern of al-fisiq, and is more dignified than al-zimmit. It is said: "Fulan is azmat al-nas," meaning the most dignified of them, and how intense is his solemnity. This is from al-Farra'. Qatadah said: In the pre-Islamic era, one of them would kill his daughter while feeding his dog. Allah rebuked them for that and threatened them with His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾.

Umar said concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: Qays ibn Asim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! I buried eight daughters who were mine in the pre-Islamic era." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a owner of camels." He said: "Then send a badanah (camel for sacrifice) for each one of them, if you wish."

As for His words, ﴿is asked﴾: the questioning of the buried girl is a rebuke to her killer, just as one says to a child when he is beaten: "Why were you beaten? What is your fault?" Al-Hasan said: Allah wished to rebuke her killer, because she was killed without any fault. Ibn Aslam said: "For what sin was she struck?" — for they used to strike her. Some scholars said concerning His words, ﴿is asked﴾: it means "is sought," as if he meant: just as blood is sought from the slain. He said: This is like His words: ﴿And the covenant of Allah was ever to be questioned﴾ [al-Ahzab: 15], meaning it would be demanded. So it is as if she is demanded from them, and it is said: "Where are your children?"

Al-Dahhak and Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn Zayd, recited: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾, so the girl clings to her father and says: "For what sin did you kill me?" and he has no excuse. This was said by Ibn Abbas, who used to recite it this way, and it is thus in the Mushaf of Ubayy (ibn Ka'b). Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The woman who kills her child will come on the Day of Resurrection with her child clinging to her breasts, smeared with his blood, and he will say: 'O Lord, this is my mother, and this is the one who killed me.'"

The first opinion is the view of the majority, and it is like His word to Jesus: ﴿Did you say to the people…﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116], by way of rebuke and reproach to them. Likewise, the questioning of the buried girl is a rebuke to the one who buried her. This is more emphatic than asking her about her killing, because that cannot be correct without a sin; so "for what sin was it done?" — when it becomes clear that she had no sin, it is greater in its severity and in the manifestation of the proof against her killer. And Allah knows best.

It was read "qutthilat" with shaddah (intensive), and this is clear evidence that the children of polytheists are not punished, and that punishment is not deserved except for a sin.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾: that is, they are opened after having been folded. The intended meaning is the pages of deeds, in which the angels wrote what its people did of good and evil. They are folded by death and unfolded on the Day of Resurrection, and each person stands before his page and knows what is in it, and says: ﴿What is this book that leaves out nothing small or great, except that it has counted it?﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].
